newsitem.title: USA: Navajo to shut N.M. refinery for maintenance.
newsitem.headline: Navajo to shut N.M. refinery for maintenance.

text.p: Navajo Refining Co. will shut its entire 60,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) refinery in Artesia, New Mexico, for five-weeks maintenance work to start September 15, refinery officials said Monday.

"All of our operating units will be turned around in sequence," a plant official said. "We're doing an extensive revamp of our cat cracker," he added, referring to the plant's main gasoline-making unit.
The catalytic or "cat" cracker, makes part of the plant's 36,000 bpd production of gasoline.
Plant officials said they will replace missing production through supply agreements that were arranged months ago.
The refinery supplies gasoline, asphalt, and diesel fuel to parts of New Mexico and Arizona.
Navajo is owned by Holly Corp.
